chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband dies, that there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for her.

key_terms.عِدّتِهَا: Her waiting period (implied by chapter title context)

ai.seo_question: Does a pregnant widow receive maintenance (nafaqah) from her deceased husband's estate in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the jurisprudential principle that a pregnant widow’s waiting period (‘iddah) concludes with childbirth rather than the passage of time, thereby terminating the husband’s obligation to provide maintenance (nafaqah) at that specific moment. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia interpretation of the intersection between gestational duration and financial entitlements, distinguishing it from the general rule for non-pregnant widows. It underscores the precision of Shia fiqh in linking legal status changes directly to biological events as derived from the Imams' teachings.
